channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ontario will soon make a driver’s licence and insurance mandatory for some e-bikes
Ontario was warned about career college with skyrocketing OSAP growth, letter shows
item.description: A career college with student financial aid usage that grew thousands of per cent in a few years was not among those the minister cut off this spring, and a letter newly obtained by The Canadian Press shows he was specifically warned about the school more than a year earlier.

item.title: Doug Ford says Ontario will look to ‘curtail’ online gambling advertisements
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says the amount of online gambling advertising across the province is 'out of control' and that his office is considering restrictions on the industry.

item.title: All drivers will be able to use Ontario HOV lanes in off-peak hours. Here is how it will work
item.description: Those driving alone will soon be able to use carpool lanes on Ontario highways during off-peak hours.

item.title: Ontario proposes mining reforms to speed up development
item.description: Ontario is proposing mining reforms to speed up development and exploration and revoke idle leases, drawing concern from First Nations leaders about consultation.

item.title: ‘It’s life or death’: Cancer patients with months to live challenge treatment denial in Ontario court
item.description: Lawyers for the provincial government tangled with lawyers for two cancer patients who were denied public funding for out-of-country treatment for their rare conditions in Ontario’s Divisional Court on Tuesday.

item.title: Ending homelessness will be 'very challenging,' Ontario Premier Doug Ford says
item.description: Ending homelessness in 10 years will be “very challenging,” Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Tuesday.

item.title: Ford backs Chow’s use of strong mayor powers to replace Toronto’s city manager
item.description: Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow is getting a vote of confidence from Premier Doug Ford following a surprise decision to use strong mayor powers to replace the city manager.

item.title: Non-profits fear housing halt as Ontario bill targets tax exemption
item.description: A legislative proposal introduced by the Ontario government as part of its Fall Economic Update is sparking alarm among non-profit housing agencies across the province.

item.title: Doug Ford ‘very confident’ Canada could see trade deal with U.S. soon
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith expressed optimism Monday that Canada could see a trade deal reached with the U.S. before the end of the year.

item.title: Minister defends not initially cutting off college with skyrocketing OSAP usage
item.description: Ontario’s minister of colleges and universities says a career college with student financial aid usage that grew thousands of per cent in a few years was not one of six he cut off in May because of the 'evolving nature of the data.'

item.title: 'Happy, exercise, help others': The secrets behind Raymond Cho's 90 years on Earth
item.description: On a recent Friday in the far eastern reaches of Toronto, Raymond Cho deftly serves a table tennis ball against a new rival, a reporter about half his age from The Canadian Press.

item.title: Navdeep Bains named new Ontario Liberal leader
item.description: Former MP Navdeep Bains eked out a narrow victory Saturday to become the next Ontario Liberal leader, pledging to focus now on uniting the party and getting it in fighting shape for the next election.

item.title: Ontario Liberals to select third new leader since 2018
item.description: Ontario Liberals wrap up a long leadership race Saturday, and, they hope, an even longer stretch without a long-term leader, as the party gets set to name the person they have selected to shepherd them into the next election.

item.title: CUPE Ontario education workers vote in favour of strike action ahead of bargaining
item.description: Ontario school board workers represented by CUPE have given their union a strike mandate, making it the fifth major education union to vote in favour of possible job action.
